summary: In 1930 the Booker T. Washington Community Center held a masquerade ball at the Scottish Rite Hall. From 1953 the city widened Geary and Webster through the district — its own engineers wrote that Webster was the first stage of a thoroughfare traversing the heart of the Western Addition redevelopment area — and went on vacating streets inside that project area for twenty years after: O'Farrell in 1961, Buchanan and Birch in 1974, O'Farrell and Ellis again in 1981. Through the 1980s the district filled with condominium projects, one of them 247 units on its own. Since 1978 it has closed Divisadero, and then Fillmore, every June for Juneteenth.
